greater_equal_.function: Write, for every element pair, A >= B into A in place; the scalar overload compares against a Python number
greater_equal_.inputs: A and B are float16 / bfloat16 / float32 tensors of identical shape on gcu, contiguous; the scalar form takes a Python number
greater_equal_.outputs: The input A, overwritten with the 0/1 comparison result in the original dtype
greater_equal_.implementation: Triton GCU400 backend: the file already carried tuned flat kernels, but aten::greater_equal_.Tensor was bound to the public greater_equal_tensor_ wrapper, which routed every call through the generic pointwise kernel and never reached them. A vendor greater_equal_tensor_ now delegates to the tuned in-place entry. In-place fp32 tiles above 2^27 elements also moved from 32768 lanes / 2 warps to 65536 lanes / 4 warps
greater_equal_.special_cases: Yes: broadcast pair and scalar forms, int64 path gated by TORCH_GCU_ENABLE_INT64_AND_UINT64, tail masks, and a 48-CTA grid cap ceiling shared by every arm
greater_equal_.results: Accuracy 102/102 passed. Benchmark average speedup 1.075x over the 15 core cases (was 0.52x). The 1 Gi float16 case moved 0.34x -> 0.98x, float32 0.73x -> 1.00x, bfloat16 0.34x -> 0.90x; the remaining sub-1.0 cells are the 1 Gi pointwise streams that already run at the memory roofline

grouped_matmul.op_category: Grouped matrix multiply / MoE expert GEMM
grouped_matmul.function: Group the rows of x[M,K] by group_list, run one GEMM per group against weight[G,K,N], and concatenate the results row-wise into out[M,N]
grouped_matmul.inputs: x[M,K] float16/bfloat16; weight[G,K,N] the same dtype; group_list[G] int32/int64; group_list_type 0 = prefix sum of row counts (last element = M), 1 = rows per group
grouped_matmul.outputs: out[M,N], with the same dtype as x
grouped_matmul.implementation: Triton (a new GCU400-specific implementation): the device derives each group's row range from group_list, assigns tiles through a flat (group, m tile, n tile) index plus a fixed 48-program stride loop, and handles non-divisible m/n/k with block_ptr + boundary_check
grouped_matmul.special_cases: Yes: M=0 returns an empty tensor directly; empty groups are skipped; K/N that are not multiples of the block are padded; both group_list_type semantics (prefix sum / counts) are supported
grouped_matmul.test_cases: tests/test_grouped_matmul.py and benchmark/test_grouped_matmul.py are gated with ascend_only upstream (the reference implementation needs torch_npu), so they are SKIPPED on enflame; this task covered the three official quick shapes (1024,2048,4096,32) / (7354,4096,1024,32) / (4096,4096,2048,32) plus three boundary shapes (including M=0) with a self-built probe
grouped_matmul.results: The official cases are SKIPPED (upstream they only run on ascend and the torch_npu reference is unavailable) -> final acceptance FAILED_FINAL_VERIFY(Skipped); the self-built probe passes correctness 12/12 (fp16/bf16 x group_list_type 0/1) and boundary 12/12
grouped_matmul.accuracy: vs the CPU float32 reference max rel 6.3e-4 (fp16 tolerance rtol 2e-2); vs the per-group vendor torch.matmul result max abs diff 0.0 (bit-identical)
grouped_matmul.performance: quick shape median latency 0.477 / 0.722 / 0.906 ms = 37.7 / 41.7 / 76.1 TFLOPS (GCU400, fixed grid 48, BM=128 BN=128 BK=512 stages=4)

linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.function: Compute the principal square root of a Hermitian positive-definite matrix V·sqrt(Lambda)·V^H and write it into out
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.inputs: inp[..., n, n] (float32 takes the fast path); out is provided by the caller
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.outputs: out, with the same shape/dtype/device as inp; returns out itself
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.implementation: Triton + vendor combination: eigh is still provided by the vendor; for n<=128 a single Triton reconstruction kernel (one tl.dot plus an upper-triangular projection for V·sqrt(Lambda)·V^H) writes straight into the out buffer; for n>128 the combined eigh + clamp/sqrt + bmm + Hermitian-projection path is kept
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.special_cases: Yes: a mismatched out shape -> warn + resize; a mismatched out dtype/device -> RuntimeError; n=0 returns directly; n>128 or non-float32 falls back to the combined path
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.results: Official accuracy 3 passed / 28 skipped (the numerical cases need torch>=2.15 for aten::linalg_matrix_sqrth and this environment runs torch 2.11 without that op), and the benchmark is skipped wholesale by an upstream skipif -> final acceptance FAILED_FINAL_VERIFY(Skipped); the self-built probe passes 9/9 (n=1/4/8/32/64/128/256 plus two batched groups) and the out variant passes 8/9 (n=1 does not hit the resize branch because the out shape already matches the input)
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.accuracy: vs the CPU float64 reference max rel 1.2e-6; the independence check S@S ~ A leaves a residual of rel 2.1e-6
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.performance: median latency for n=1/4/8/32/64/128 is 0.198/0.332/0.389/0.684/1.028/1.794 ms, of which vendor eigh takes 0.095/0.103/0.138/0.343/0.671/1.507 ms; the out variant is another 1.02-1.14x faster than the non-out version (one staging allocation and copy saved)
linalg_matrix_sqrth_out.speedup: 1.46x / 1.53x / 1.55x / 1.41x / 1.32x / 1.15x, mean 1.35x (baseline = the pre-fix eigh + vendor combined implementation; n=256 takes the combined path at 1.01x)

sparse_sampled_addmm.op_category: Sparse sampled matrix multiply (CSR input, sampled_addmm)
sparse_sampled_addmm.function: out.values() = alpha * (mat1 @ mat2)[sampled positions of the CSR structure] + beta * input.values(), batched over the leading dimensions
sparse_sampled_addmm.inputs: input: sparse_csr float16/bfloat16/float32 (batch, M, N) with int32 or int64 indices; mat1 (batch, M, K) and mat2 (batch, K, N) in the same dtype on gcu; alpha/beta scalars
sparse_sampled_addmm.outputs: A CSR tensor with the same structure and dtype as input (or the provided out tensor)
sparse_sampled_addmm.implementation: Triton GCU400 backend, three-stage pipeline: build the slot map or the dense scratch, run the dense product with tl.dot, then fold the tile onto the value slots (dense scratch + gather, or direct scatter). This round widened the K block of 16-bit dots from 64 to 128 with two stages, which removes the MMA pipeline stall the shared bmm table leaves behind
sparse_sampled_addmm.special_cases: Yes: 0/1 sparsity, empty groups, alpha=0 and K=0 early exit, batch broadcasting of a 2-D CSR input, non-contiguous mat1/mat2, int32 and int64 indices, grid.x ceiling of 65535, DSM and slot-map budgets
sparse_sampled_addmm.test_cases: tests/test_sparse_sampled_addmm.py (all nodes, standard protocol, no CPU-fallback env), benchmark/test_sparse_sampled_addmm.py at --level core
sparse_sampled_addmm.results: Standard run without ENFLAME_PT_OP_DEBUG_CONFIG=fallback_cpu=all_ops passes: accuracy 1440/1440 nodes, benchmark average speedup 0.815x over the 15 core cases (0.703x before this round's K-block change). 16-bit cells improved 5-20% in absolute latency, e.g. (16,2048,2048) 6.096 -> 5.260 ms and (16,4096,4096) 32.464 -> 26.466 ms

sparse_sampled_addmm_out.function: out.values() = alpha * (mat1 @ mat2)[sampled positions of the CSR structure] + beta * input.values(), batched over the leading dimensions
sparse_sampled_addmm_out.inputs: input: sparse_csr float16/bfloat16/float32 (batch, M, N) with int32 or int64 indices; mat1 (batch, M, K) and mat2 (batch, K, N) in the same dtype on gcu; alpha/beta scalars
sparse_sampled_addmm_out.outputs: A CSR tensor with the same structure and dtype as input (or the provided out tensor)

This round widened the K block of 16-bit dots from 64 to 128 with two stages, which removes the MMA pipeline stall the shared bmm table leaves behind
sparse_sampled_addmm_out.special_cases: Yes: 0/1 sparsity, empty groups, alpha=0 and K=0 early exit, batch broadcasting of a 2-D CSR input, non-contiguous mat1/mat2, int32 and int64 indices, grid.x ceiling of 65535, DSM and slot-map budgets
sparse_sampled_addmm_out.test_cases: tests/test_sparse_sampled_addmm.py (all nodes, standard protocol, no CPU-fallback env), benchmark/test_sparse_sampled_addmm.py at --level core
sparse_sampled_addmm_out.results: Standard run without ENFLAME_PT_OP_DEBUG_CONFIG=fallback_cpu=all_ops passes: accuracy 90/90 nodes, benchmark 15/15 core cases OK with average speedup 0.684x (fp16 0.617x, fp32 0.756x, bf16 0.678x). The previous record could not be reproduced on the board: the benchmark loop aborted with a 140.53 GiB / 144.00 GiB GCU OOM and reported performance NOTFOUND, because the out variant rebuilt a whole sparse tensor per call and the torch_gcu front end leaks about nnz*8 bytes of device memory whenever torch.sparse_csr_tensor is built from freshly allocated index/value tensors. The out variant now seeds out.values() in place (0.0 MiB growth over 40 calls on 4x4096x4096x128 fp32), and no kernel or dispatch behaviour is changed
